title: 2002 AMC 12B Problem 13
statement: The sum of \(18\) consecutive positive integers is a perfect square. The smallest possible value of this sum is

solutions.text:
The sum of \(n,\) \(n+1,\ldots,\) \(n+17\) is \(18n+\dfrac{17\cdot18}{2}=9(2n+17).\) Since \(9\) is a perfect square, \(2n+17\) must be one too.

The smallest positive integer \(n\) making \(2n+17\) a perfect square is \(n=4,\) giving \(2n+17=25\) and a sum of \(9\cdot25=225.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Since \(9\) is already a square, \(2n+17\) must be an odd perfect square; take the smallest valid one
